Re: Closing of Representation — Okonkwo v. Fallbrook Freight Systems, LLC, No. 3:25-cv-04412 (M.D. Tenn.)

Dear Ms. Okonkwo:

Thank you for allowing us to represent you in this matter. This letter confirms that our representation of you has ended as of today, April 14, 2026, and explains what that means and what you should do next.

1. Scope of what we did. We represented you in the matter identified above, from our engagement letter dated August 2, 2025 through the entry of the order of dismissal on April 2, 2026. Our representation covered that matter only. We did not represent you in any other matter, and we have no continuing duty to advise you about any other matter.

2. We no longer represent you. We are not your lawyers in this or any other matter as of the date of this letter. We will take no further action on your behalf, and no lawyer at this firm is monitoring any deadline for you.

3. Deadlines you must now watch yourself. This is the most important part of this letter. Any appeal from the April 2, 2026 order of dismissal must be filed within thirty (30) days of entry of that order — that is, by May 4, 2026. We are not filing an appeal. If you wish to appeal, you must retain new counsel or act on your own behalf before that date. A missed deadline generally cannot be cured. There may be other deadlines, including statutes of limitation on related claims, that we have not identified, and you should have new counsel review them promptly.

4. Your file. The complete file in this matter is yours. We are enclosing it with this letter on a USB drive, and a paper copy is available on request at no charge. We will retain a copy for seven (7) years from today, after which it may be destroyed without further notice to you. If you want us to hold it longer, write to us before April 14, 2033.

5. Fees and trust funds. Your account is paid in full and no fees are outstanding. We are enclosing a check for $1,480.00, which is the unearned balance remaining in our trust account for this matter, together with a final accounting of all receipts and disbursements from that account, as Tennessee Rule of Professional Conduct 1.15 requires.

6. Confidentiality. Our duty to keep your confidences continues after this representation ends and does not expire.

7. New counsel. We will cooperate promptly with any lawyer you retain, and we will transfer the file and answer questions at no charge to you.

We are grateful for the opportunity to have served you. If any part of this letter is unclear, please call me before you act.

Very truly yours,

BRIGHTWATER & OSEI LLP

/s/ Priya Osei
Priya Osei
Enclosures: file on USB drive; trust check no. 4412; final trust accounting
